absent: Central select waiting engine scanning and deadline sleep behavior beyond its call signature
Shared timeout construction, accuracy estimation and remaining time update mechanics
Signal mask installation and compat mask translation semantics
Poll wait queue setup, interruptible sleep and teardown behavior
File poll dispatch, busy loop enablement and timing support
Descriptor set import, clearing and export helper implementations
Sequential file iterator read, position traversal, buffer acquisition, commit and overflow handling
Path rendering, string escape and hex formatting helper implementations
Lifecycle of slab cache and single-entry sequence callbacks beyond start and show

findings.text: Central select service accepts a descriptor count with three optional caller sets and an optional absolute deadline. Counts beyond the sampled table maximum are reduced to that maximum. Small bitmap needs use stack storage while larger needs use dynamic storage with overflow protection. Successful completion reports ready descriptor total with result maps exported. Empty unsignaled waits report zero while empty signaled waits report restartable interruption. Invalid counts, allocation exhaustion and result export faults map to distinct negative errors, and dynamic storage is released on all exits.

Legacy timeout wrapper treats absent timeval as unbounded wait. Present values with negative components are rejected as invalid before any conversion, preventing wrapped deadlines. Valid values are normalized into seconds plus nanoseconds and turned into an absolute deadline through shared timeout logic. The central select service is then used and remaining time handling is delegated to shared finish logic.
Classic select system entry receives descriptor count with three user set references and a timeval reference, delegating entirely to the legacy timeout wrapper and returning its outcome.

Shared pselect logic supports absent timeout as unbounded wait and present timeout in native or old 32-bit form with bad address reported for faulty reads. Deadlines are built through shared timeout logic with invalid values rejected. Caller signal masks are installed before waiting, with installation failures aborting the wait. Final status and remaining time are produced through shared finish logic keyed by original timeout form.
Mask carrier aggregates a user signal set reference together with its length, enabling a single user pointer to convey an optional mask.

Carrier import preserves a preinitialized empty value when the source pointer is null. Otherwise both fields are fetched with fault tolerance that yields bad address on failure, using a path tuned for frequent invocation.

Two modern pselect entries each start from an empty mask carrier, import caller mask data with bad address on fault, then use shared pselect logic. One interprets timeouts as native layout and the other as old 32-bit layout.
Legacy packed argument block aggregates descriptor count with three user set references for distinct interest classes plus a timeval reference for timeout.
Single-pointer legacy select entry copies a packed argument block from user space with bad address on fault, then forwards its unpacked fields to the legacy timeout wrapper.
Poll storage chunk links to an optional successor, records how many descriptors it holds, and carries a counted flexible array of those descriptors, supporting chaining of stack and heap chunks.
Heap chunk capacity is specified as page size less header size divided by one descriptor size, governing how many descriptors each heap extension holds.

Per-descriptor poll evaluation treats negative numbers as no event and unresolvable files as invalid. Caller interest is combined with error and hangup conditions for the file query, including an optional busy indication. Busy capability is reported separately when observed, and only conditions within caller interest are retained.

Poll waiter occupies immediate, scanning, busy and sleeping phases. Zero deadlines enter immediate mode without waiter registration. Scanning visits every chunk and disables further registration after first readiness. Absent readiness surfaces waiter error or restartable interruption when signals are pending. Busy-capable sockets allow bounded spinning while rescheduling is unneeded. Otherwise an expiry is materialized lazily with accuracy slack and interruptible sleep continues until readiness or timeout.
Stack descriptor capacity is specified as stack buffer size less header size divided by one descriptor size, bounding the fast path without heap use.

Poll core accepts descriptor totals within the file limit and rejects larger totals as invalid. Input descriptors are gathered into a stack head plus page-sized heap extensions with bad address on faulty reads and no memory on allocation failure. Wait state is initialized around engine execution, readiness flags are written back to user space, heap extensions are released on all exits, and the engine count or fault status is returned.
Poll restart logic resumes waiting from saved user pointer, count and optional deadline, reusing poll core. Restartable interruption causes rearming of the same restart logic.

Millisecond poll entry interprets negative timeouts as unbounded wait and non-negative values as deadlines built from seconds plus nanoseconds. After poll core execution, restartable interruption triggers preservation of user pointer, count and deadline presence into restart state with restart armed.

Two ppoll entries accept descriptor arrays with optional timeout and signal mask. Timeouts in native or old 32-bit form are imported with bad address on fault and converted to deadlines with invalid rejected. Signal masks are installed before waiting, poll core is used, and remaining time is finalized according to original timeout form.
Compat bitmap granularity equals eight times the compat word size, defining how many descriptor bits each compat word represents.

Compat bitmap transfer treats null user references as zero fill on import and success without action on export. Non-null references move the requested bit count between compat user words and native words.

Compat select core provides the same contract as native central select with clamping to sampled maximum, stack fast path and array allocation fallback, compat bitmap import with result clearing, engine execution, restartable interruption for empty signaled waits, and compat bitmap export with bad address on fault.

Compat select timeout handling treats absent old timeval as unbounded wait. Present values are copied with bad address on fault, normalized from seconds plus microseconds into deadline form through shared logic with invalid rejected, then compat select core is used with remaining time finalized in old timeval form.
Compat packed block aggregates descriptor count with four compat-sized pointer fields for three sets plus timeout, each requiring translation to native pointers before use.

Compat select entries delegate to shared compat select timeout handling. The direct form forwards compat set and timeval references unchanged. The old form first copies a compat packed block with bad address on fault and translates each pointer field before forwarding.

Compat pselect logic supports absent timeout and present timeout in old or native form with bad address on faulty reads. Deadlines use shared conversion with invalid rejected. Compat signal masks are installed before waiting, compat select core is used, and remaining time is finalized in original form. Unexpected timeout forms are fatal.
Compat mask carrier aggregates a compat pointer field with a compat length field, mirroring the native carrier for compat callers.
Compat carrier import preserves prior contents when source is null and otherwise fetches both fields with fault handling that yields bad address on failure.

Four compat time-specific entries cover pselect with 64-bit and 32-bit timeouts plus ppoll with 32-bit and 64-bit timeouts. Pselect forms import a compat mask carrier with bad address on fault and translate its pointer before using shared compat pselect logic. Ppoll forms import timeout directly, install compat masks, use poll core, and finalize remaining time in matching layout.
Logging prefix for this sequential file module is defined from the build module name followed by caller format, ensuring consistent message tagging.
Sequential file slab cache pointer resides in memory that becomes read-only after initialization, preventing later modification.

Sequential file read entry adapts classic read parameters to iterator form using a single destination segment and synchronous control, synchronizes file position in both directions around iterator execution, and returns its transferred count or error.

Sequential file positioning supports absolute and relative origins only, rejecting other origins and negative results as invalid. Targets equal to current read position update file position directly. Other targets repeatedly traverse until stable, resetting file position and sequence counters on traversal failure and committing read and file positions on success.
All position evaluation, traversal and commit steps for sequential file seeking execute while holding the sequence mutex, with release on every exit path.
Descriptor table maximum sampling in both native and compat select cores occurs under RCU read protection with prompt release, ensuring a stable snapshot despite concurrent table growth.

Buffered textual append helpers add escaped memory, binary-format expansion or plain strings to the sequence buffer. Each respects remaining capacity and marks overflow when output would exceed available space rather than truncating silently.
File path formatter renders the path associated with a given open file into the sequence buffer using a caller escape set, delegating to shared path rendering.

Hexadecimal dump helper normalizes row width to supported values, emits one line per row with address, offset or plain prefix as selected, renders bytes through shared hex formatting into sequence buffer space with overflow marking, and terminates each row with newline until input exhausted or overflow observed.
Single-entry sequence iteration advances the supplied position and always terminates after the current item, while its stop operation performs no action.

List position helpers locate the element at a given index by linear walk, with plain and RCU traversal variants. Head-inclusive forms return the list head itself for index zero and otherwise start from index minus one. The RCU next helper advances position and maps wrap to the head into termination.

Hash list position helpers locate nodes by linear walk. The head-inclusive start returns a dedicated start token for index zero and otherwise offsets by one. The next helper advances position, yielding the first node after the start token or the successor link otherwise.

Legacy timeval seconds summing in signed arithmetic could wrap crafted negative inputs into apparently valid positive deadlines with saturation to effectively infinite waits. Explicit rejection of negative components before normalization preserves required invalid reporting.

Six-fold bitmap sizing could overflow addressable range for extreme descriptor counts. Pre-multiplication comparison against maximum representable size divided by six plus stack threshold checks ensures oversized requests fail safely with no memory rather than wrapping.

Descriptor counts above the file resource limit are rejected outright for poll, while select counts are clamped to a once-sampled table maximum. Single sampling avoids races where concurrent growth could otherwise cause inconsistent bounds during bitmap sizing and scanning.

Zero readiness coexisting with pending signals must not be reported as successful timeout. Mapping such cases to restartable interruption preserves signal delivery and restart semantics across select, compat select and poll engines.
